source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A decision made with fairly little attention paid at all to the client's actual clinical bleeding status observed directly at the bedside during rounds each shift","B":"Automatically correcting any abnormal coagulation lab value that is observed, whether or not the client actually shows any outward signs of active bleeding","C":"Careful clinical judgment, since coagulation lab values in liver disease do not always directly correlate with actual bleeding risk, and unnecessary correction carries its own risks","D":"Fairly few clinical considerations actually being unique to liver disease when a provider makes this particular treatment decision for a given client"}}
source_row.rationale: Blood product administration in liver disease involves careful clinical judgment, since coagulation lab values (such as INR) in liver disease do not always directly correlate with actual bleeding risk given the complex, often balanced nature of liver disease-related coagulopathy, and unnecessary correction carries its own risks (such as volume overload or transfusion reactions).
source_row.source_detail: Clinical Judgment in Blood Product Decisions
